tagline: Enabling a more sustainable and resource-efficient future with technology leadership in electrification and automation.
hero_kpi_rationale: Operational EBITA of $5.4 billion, up 20%, reflects ABB's operational excellence and ability to generate value in a complex macroeconomic environment, supported by improved industrial efficiency and price revaluation.
company_description: ABB Ltd provides electrification, motion, and automation solutions and products for customers in utilities, industry and transport, and infrastructure in Europe, the Americas, Asia, the Middle East, and Africa. The company operates through Electrification, Motion, and Automation segments. Its Electrification segment offers renewable power solutions, modular substation packages, distribution automation products, switchboards and panelboards, switchgears, UPS solutions, circuit breakers, measuring and sensing devices, control products, wiring accessories, enclosures and cabling systems, and intelligent home and building solutions. The company's Motion segment designs, manufactures, and sells drives, motors, generators, and traction converters that are driving the low-carbon future for industries, cities, infrastructure, and transportation. The company's Automation segment offers industry-specific, integrated automation, electrification and digital solutions, as well as lifecycle services for the process, hybrid and marine industries. kpis.name: Adjusted operating profit
kpis.explanation: Adjusted operating profit, excluding exceptional items.
kpis.description: Operational EBITA reached $5.427 billion, up 20% at comparable rates, reflecting improved industrial efficiency.
kpis.signal: Strong increase in operating margin, indicating solid execution.

kpis.name: New orders received
kpis.explanation: Total value of new orders signed during the year.
kpis.description: Orders amounted to $33.818 billion, down 1% year-on-year, but up 3% at comparable rates.
kpis.signal: Order stability despite a challenging macro environment.

kpis.name: Order backlog
kpis.explanation: Value of unfulfilled orders at year-end.
kpis.description: Order backlog reached $21.567 billion, up 9%, supported by demand in automation and electrification.
kpis.signal: Backlog growing strongly, a positive indicator for future revenues.

kpis.name: Revenues
kpis.description: Revenues reached $32.235 billion, up 9%, or 14% at comparable rates.
kpis.signal: Solid growth driven by price increases and demand.

kpis.name: Gross margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of goods sold, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross margin is estimated at approximately 38.5%, up 1.6 percentage points, driven by price revaluation and industrial efficiency.
kpis.signal: Gross margin improvement due to pricing power.

kpis.name: Research and development investments
kpis.explanation: Annual expenses dedicated to research and development.
kpis.description: R&D spending amounted to $1.3 billion, stable compared to the prior year, supporting innovation in automation and electrification.
kpis.signal: R&D maintained at high levels despite cost pressures.

kpis.name: Capital expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending on fixed assets to maintain and expand production capacity.
kpis.description: Capital expenditures amounted to approximately $800 million, stable compared to 2022.
kpis.signal: Moderate Capex, consistent with a mature industrial model.

kpis.name: Total headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of full-time employees at year-end.
kpis.description: ABB employs 107,900 people, up 3%, supporting organic growth and innovation.
kpis.signal: Headcount increasing, signaling expansion in key markets.

kpis.name: Women in senior management
kpis.explanation: Proportion of women in senior management roles (Hay grades 1-7).
kpis.description: The share of women in senior management reached 21%, up 3.2 percentage points, exceeding the 20% target.

risks.title: Intense competition in technology markets
risks.summary: ABB faces increasing competition from large industrial groups and new entrants, particularly in automation, electrification, and robotics, putting pressure on pricing and innovation.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned in the enterprise risk management (ERM) section, with strong language on competitive pressure. It is stable over time and relevant to ABB's technology sector. The Competition category is strategic for the business.

risks.title: Dependence on global supply chains
risks.summary: Global supply chain disruptions, particularly in electronic components and semiconductors, have affected ABB's ability to deliver products on time, especially in automation and robotics.
risks.score_rationale: This risk was top of ERM concerns in 2021, with strong language ('severe constraints'). It shows an upward trend and directly impacts production and delivery. High weight in industrial operations.

risks.title: Increasing cybersecurity regulations
risks.summary: Growing regulatory requirements on cybersecurity, especially for connected industrial systems, require ABB to strengthen the security of its software and platforms, under risk of loss of trust or penalties.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is integrated into ERM assessments and linked to ABB's digital products. Language is preventive but emphasizes exposure. Upward trend with digitalization. Key category for connected solutions.

risks.title: Separation and spin-off of strategic divisions
risks.summary: Separation activities of certain businesses, such as electric vehicle charging or turbocharging, present organizational, technological, and valuation challenges for ABB.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly cited in ERM (preparation for spin-off of charging and turbocharging). Language marked by uncertainty. New or rising. High impact on technological structure.

risks.title: Dependence on key industrial partners
risks.summary: ABB maintains significant commercial relationships with partners such as Fluor (customer) and Hitachi Energy (supplier and customer), creating interdependencies that could affect industrial project continuity.
risks.score_rationale: The link with Fluor and Hitachi Energy is documented in board member relationships. Language is moderate ('not unusual'), but real exposure. Stable. Moderate operational risk.

risks.title: Cybersecurity of connected industrial systems
risks.summary: ABB's increasingly connected automation and electrification systems are exposed to cyberattacks, potentially causing major operational outages for industrial customers.
risks.score_rationale: Central risk in ABB's digital products. Strong language on growing threats. Upward trend. Critical category for customer trust and operational continuity.

risks.title: Technological innovation and intellectual property protection
risks.summary: ABB's ability to innovate and protect its patents in robotics, industrial AI, and automation is crucial to maintaining its competitive edge against global players.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is implicit in technological competition and mentioned through innovation challenges. Language is indirect but logical for the sector. Stable. High weight in product differentiation.

ai_positioning.summary: ABB is gradually integrating artificial intelligence into its automation and predictive maintenance solutions, particularly within the Robotics & Discrete Automation division, without making AI a central pillar of its strategy. AI is used to optimize machine and industrial process performance.
evidence: Focus on artificial intelligence in Robotics & Discrete Automation division
AI work in machine automation and factory automation
AI used in predictive maintenance and digital twin applications
